artifact: BF16 launch-variance supplement to the KL analysis
question: what is the expected BF16->FP8 / BF16->FP4 KL over BF16 launch identity, how much of its uncertainty is launch-to-launch, and does the effect stay resolvable once that is carried?

contract_position.bf16_launch_treated_as: nuisance variance component / crossed repeated measure
contract_position.G2_G2prime_status: historical outcomes and thresholds preserved unchanged; this analysis supplements them and re-adjudicates nothing

BF16||FP8.direction: worse -- the floor is a LARGER fraction of the signal under this estimator

BF16||FP4.direction: better -- the floor is a smaller fraction of the signal

contract_position.against: EXPERIMENTAL_CONTRACT.md quality-run validity: `no result was averaged or re-referenced to convert a failure into a pass`

marginal_step_is_unaffected.why: the project's marginal quantity is measured with FP8 as the reference and contains no BF16 distribution at all, so BF16 launch identity cannot enter it. The whole nuisance-variance problem is confined to the BF16-anchored pairs.

other_fp8_fp4_distributions_considered_a.results/quality/gates/engine_profile/: 4 traj x 10 pos x 2 launches per config under graph_2048 -- the tempting near-miss. Barred twice over: its manifest carries KL_SPEC 4ef13273db16d285, not the current spec, and its provisional_trajectories.json holds different continuations from the frozen set, so the contexts are not the same contexts.
other_fp8_fp4_distributions_considered_a.results/quality/gates/cache_equivalence/: prefix caching off -- a different engine profile; and no FP8 arm.
other_fp8_fp4_distributions_considered_a.results/qualification/logits/: fp16 storage (fails G4), single position, historical prototype path.
other_fp8_fp4_distributions_considered_a.results/pilot/gate_logits/: fp16 storage, position 1 only, self-described as a pre-timing trip-wire and not a quality result.

statistical_unit: trajectory; BF16 launch is a crossed repeated-measure factor

bf16_launch_sources.provenance: P10 smoke; the only BF16 launch collected on the same 40-context grid as the FP8/FP4 distributions

keys_that_cannot_match_by_construction.substitute: per-cell context_sha256 equality over the shared cells, asserted above

exchangeability_preconditions.engine_identity_hash_is_not_a_launch_non: it hashes deterministic configuration properties only; it cannot distinguish launches. matrix_sha256 is what establishes independence.
exchangeability_preconditions.collection_git_head_note: the launches were collected at different commits. Only new files and a 2-line gates.py edit separate them; collect_kl.py, qengine.py, positions.py, kl_math.py and qcommon.py -- the whole collection path -- are byte-identical across the two.
exchangeability_preconditions.session_confound: launch identity is confounded with SESSION: the launches were not all collected in one sitting, so the launch variance component absorbs any between-session drift and rests on fewer independent sessions than launches.

grid_regime_check.question: does the smoke's 40-context grid put its BF16 launch in a different regime from the 640-context floor64 launches?
grid_regime_check.structural_argument: trajectories 0-3 are scored first in both regimes, from an identical cold engine, in identical submission order (one trajectory of ten nested contexts per generate call), with identical num_gpu_blocks and kv_cache_tokens and zero preemptions. KV eviction in the 640-context grid begins far later than trajectory 3 and cannot propagate backwards, so the regime difference is causally downstream of the cells used here.
grid_regime_check.statistic: launch leverage -- the mean divergence from one launch to every other
grid_regime_check.power_caveat: with 4 launches the smallest attainable rank p-value is 0.25, so this test CANNOT reject exchangeability at 0.05 and a moderate regime effect would go undetected. It rules out a gross effect, nothing finer.
grid_regime_check.verdict: no gross regime effect: cross-regime mean 2.221e-04 against a largest within-regime pair of 3.432e-04, and S ranks 3 of 4 on leverage. The launches are pooled.
grid_regime_check.what_this_cannot_rule_out: a regime effect common to all launches shifts every BF16 realization together and is invisible to any between-launch comparison; and a moderate effect is beyond this test's power. Only a floor64-scale FP8/FP4 collection (P13) closes either.

bf16_to_bf16.quantity: D_KL(B_a || B_b) over ordered BF16 launch pairs -- the replication floor

launch_level_uncertainty.method: delete-one-launch jackknife; the ordered pairs are a U-statistic over launches, not R(R-1) independent levels
launch_level_uncertainty.ci_95_note: the symmetric interval's lower end fell below zero, which a divergence cannot reach; reported clamped, with the raw value beside it
launch_level_uncertainty.why: treating the ordered pairs as independent levels would report df=R(R-1)-1 where the design has R-1, and understate the floor's own uncertainty

bf16_to_bf16.no_variance_component_reported_because: the ordered pairs share launches, so they are not independent levels of a random factor; a crossed ANOVA over them would report a df it does not have
bf16_to_bf16.relationship_to_G2_prime: this recomputes the same quantity G2' adjudicated. G2' and its 1% bound are historical and unchanged; nothing here re-adjudicates them

launch_level_uncertainty.method: delete-one-launch jackknife over the ordered-pair headlines

replication_floor_source.used_for: the side-by-side floor column only; never subtracted
replication_floor_source.n4_figure_note: the superseded n=4 floor estimate of 2.984e-04 was called a high draw from a noisy sample. At the launch level it sits INSIDE the production floor's own 95% interval, so `5.6% of the FP8 signal` is really a range, not a point.

BF16||FP8.estimator: mean over BF16 launches of the per-launch headline; each per-launch headline is the pre-registered mean of per-trajectory means
BF16||FP8.NOT_THE_HEADLINE: EVALUATION_RIG.md A.1 locks headline_KL as the mean of 64 per-trajectory means under ONE reference launch, and that remains the point estimate. This is a supplementary expected value over launch identity; the per-launch headlines are reported beside it and this number must never be rendered as `the BF16->Q KL`.

expected_mean_squares.E[MS_residual]: sigma2_E = sigma2_{AxS} + sigma2_{AxSxP}/P, NOT measurement noise

variance_components.var_level_upper_95_rule: sigma2_A <= MS_A*(R-1)/(T*chi2_{0.05,R-1}), using sigma2_E >= 0. One-sided; the only honest summary at this df.
variance_components.f_level_note: MS_level/MS_residual on (df_level, df_residual). Tests whether the level effect is separable from the level x trajectory interaction at all.
variance_components.var_theta_rule: (MS_level + MS_trajectory - MS_residual)/(R*T), the ANOVA-unbiased Var(mean); its Satterthwaite df is the honest df of the whole estimate

launch_component.primary: F ratio and the one-sided 95% upper bound; the point estimate is reported beside them and must not be quoted alone at this df
launch_component.df_caveat: sigma2_A carries 3 df. Its 95% multiplicative interval is [0.27, 39.5] at 2 df and [0.32, 13.9] at 3 df; reaching +/-30% on SE_launch would need R=37, which is not reachable here.

trajectory_component.method: pre-registered percentile bootstrap over trajectories, applied to the launch-averaged per-trajectory means
trajectory_component.estimates: (sigma2_S + sigma2_E/R)/T, the non-launch part of Var(theta)
trajectory_component.different_estimand_from_committed_artifa: the committed single-launch bootstrap estimates (sigma2_S + sigma2_E)/T; this one estimates (sigma2_S + sigma2_E/R)/T. They differ by sigma2_E(1-1/R)/T and are NOT the same interval, so no comparability with earlier artifacts is claimed
trajectory_component.finite_sample_note: the nonparametric bootstrap of a mean carries a (T-1)/T divisor, so at T=4 it understates the SD by 13.4%

anova_unbiased.rule: (MS_level + MS_trajectory - MS_residual)/(R*T), the ANOVA-unbiased Var(mean); its Satterthwaite df is the honest df of the whole estimate
anova_unbiased.preferred: this is the single-expression total with one trackable df; the bootstrap-plus-launch form below is reported because the bootstrap is the pre-registered method

bootstrap_plus_launch.rule: the percentile interval is SCALED about the point estimate by sqrt(1 + var_launch/var_bootstrap); the launch component is thereby treated as symmetric while the trajectory skew is preserved
bootstrap_plus_launch.orthogonality: the two variances add because A_r is a single constant shared by every trajectory, so no trajectory resampling can see it. This holds by the assumed independence of A from (S,E), not by construction. Note the naive s^2 over the R launch headlines would double-count sigma2_E/(RT) against the bootstrap term; (MS_A - MS_E)/T is what avoids that.

scaling_law.prediction: SD_launch(config) = sigma_proj * sqrt(2 * signal(config)); CV_launch falls as 1/sqrt(signal)
scaling_law.caution: SD(per-launch headlines) is sqrt(sigma2_A + sigma2_E/T), NOT sigma_A. It is the right input here because the law predicts the observable spread, but it must not be quoted as the launch variance component.

vs_replication_floor.interpretation: ratio is a reproducibility diagnostic only; read value_nats for magnitude. No materiality threshold is applied here.
vs_replication_floor.ratio_drifts_with_R: averaging R launches shrinks the launch noise in the numerator by sqrt(R) while the denominator stays a two-launch quantity, so this ratio moves with a design parameter. Read R beside it.
vs_replication_floor.note: the floor is reported beside the estimate and is never subtracted from it; G2/G2' adjudicate the floor and are unchanged by this analysis

pooling_evidence.statistic: rank of the odd-grid launch's per-launch headline among all launches
pooling_evidence.caveat: the odd launch's 40-context grid is perfectly confounded with launch identity for that one level, so an extreme rank cannot be attributed. With R=4 this statistic cannot reach p<0.5 for a two-sided extreme; it is disclosure, not a test. R=3 -- the launches that share a grid regime -- is the reported variant for this reason.

reproduces_committed_smoke_headline.why_not_bit_identical: the interpreter that produced results/quality/ is not the one running now (the artifact records python 3.12.13 with torch and vLLM importable; neither is true here), so np.log/np.exp inside kl_nats differ in their last bits. An exact fsum over the 40 cells reproduces THIS value, not the committed one, so the difference is in the per-cell KL values rather than in the reduction order.

resolvability.form: interval comparison; no floor is subtracted anywhere

signal.criterion: the lower end of the launch-inflated interval, taken at the ONE-SIDED 95% UPPER bound on the launch variance, still exceeds the floor

floor.phi_used: the PRODUCTION floor headline (64 trajectories, 3 launches), with the delete-one-launch jackknife interval. Means are comparable across grid sizes; no worst-cell comparison is reported anywhere here, because a maximum is an extreme-value statistic and 40-cell and 640-cell maxima are not comparable.

per_trajectory_ratio.definition: mean over trajectories of (BF16->Q KL) / (BF16->BF16 KL), both on the SAME trajectories -- a ratio, not a difference, and not a subtraction
per_trajectory_ratio.phi_used: the launch-pair-averaged BF16->BF16 KL on THESE trajectories, a different quantity from the production floor headline above
per_trajectory_ratio.launch_coverage: none -- the same BF16 launches enter both arms, so this is conditional on the launch set and its interval covers trajectory sampling only

resolvability.does_not_address_G2_prime: averaging launches shrinks the FIRST-order launch nuisance by sqrt(R) and leaves the SECOND-order floor untouched -- they are different functionals of the same perturbation. No value of R moves the G2' ratio in the direction of a pass, and this analysis is not an argument that it should.

scale_limit.bf16_to_bf16_scale: production: 64 trajectories x 10 positions x 3 launches
scale_limit.bf16_to_quantized_scale: 4 trajectories x 10 positions x 4 BF16 launches
scale_limit.why: FP8/FP4 full-vocabulary distributions exist only on the P10 smoke's 4 trajectories. P13 would supply 64 and is not authorised.
scale_limit.consequence: every BF16->FP8 / BF16->FP4 number here is n=4 in trajectories and is NOT a result. The estimator, its tests and its behaviour on real artifacts are what this delivers.

BF16||FP8.caveat: components estimated at n=4 trajectories with 3 df on the launch term and 3 on the trajectory term; indicative, not a measurement
BF16||FP8.pre_registerable_prediction: the scaling law predicts the BF16 launch CV at production scale from sigma_proj pooled across configurations: SD_launch = sigma_proj*sqrt(2*signal). Registering that before P13 turns P13 into a test of the nuisance model rather than a first look at it.

BF16||FP4.caveat: components estimated at n=4 trajectories with 3 df on the launch term and 3 on the trajectory term; indicative, not a measurement
BF16||FP4.pre_registerable_prediction: the scaling law predicts the BF16 launch CV at production scale from sigma_proj pooled across configurations: SD_launch = sigma_proj*sqrt(2*signal). Registering that before P13 turns P13 into a test of the nuisance model rather than a first look at it.
